newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Hydro says US magnesium near EU anti-dumping level.
newsitem.headline: Hydro says US magnesium near EU anti-dumping level.

text.p: Hydro Magnesium, a unit of Norwegian conglomerate Norsk Hydro, said on Wednesday U.S. producers were selling magnesium in the European Union at levels close to those that triggered anti-dumping procedures against Russian and Ukrainian exporters.

"U.S. producers are now selling in Europe at prices close to the minimum established by the European Commission for Russian and Ukrainian magnesium, and well below their transaction levels in the U.S.," Hydro said in a statement announcing price cuts.

"There are two criteria for dumping. One is that you sell below cost, which is not possible to suggest here. The second is that you sell below the price in your home market. The latter seems to apply," Hydro Magnesium Vice President in charge of marketing Robert Edgar told Reuters.
Edgar said there were market rumours that price information was being collected on both Western and Chinese magnesium producers ahead of a new European Commission inquiry.
"These are rumours in the market place which we cannot substantiate until something is announced," Edgar said.
Hydro was classed along with U.S. firms as a non-European producer in the eyes of the Commission because Norway was not a member of the European Union, he noted.
A spokesman for the EU magnesium industry association, Euroalliages, was unavailable to comment.
